item.title: 2027: Nigeria is boiling, Tinubu must douse tension now — Turaki
item.description: …Accuses APC of using violence, courts to weaken opposition …Cites declining confidence in INEC, judiciary …Jerry Gana urges President to act as father of the nation, not partisan politician By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Interim National Working Committee, Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, SAN, has urged President Bola Tinubu to urgently address rising political tension and violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that Nigeria could descend into crisis if the situation is allowed to deteriorate. Turaki said attacks on opposition politicians, intimidation of voters and declining public confidence in electoral institutions were threatening the credibility of the elections, insisting that no political ambition was worth the survival of the country. He spoke at a press conference in Abuja, where he presented a statement titled, The Country Is Boiling; Can We Reduce the Temperature? The PDP’s Interim National Working Committee, accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of shrinking the political space, encouraging attacks on opposition parties and using the judiciary to undermine political competition. Drawing parallels with the First and Second Republics, Turaki warned that the suppression of opposition parties and manipulation of electoral processes had contributed to political instability and democratic collapse in Nigeria’s past. Citing Yiaga Africa’s third National Voting Intentions Survey, released on October 7, 2026, he said 84 per cent of Nigerians were willing to vote, but 61 per cent feared violence could keep them away from polling stations. Only 34 per cent expressed confidence in the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), while 63 per cent had little or no confidence in the judiciary’s ability to resolve electoral disputes fairly. The PDP chairman cited alleged attacks on supporters of Peter Obi, the ADC presidential campaign of Atiku Abubakar and activist Omoyele Sowore, including incidents in Delta, Sokoto and Ekiti states. He accused APC-linked operatives of being behind the incidents, while also alleging that opposition parties were being weakened through politically motivated court cases and voter intimidation. He further accused some public officials of threatening voters with displacement if they failed to support the APC, warning that such actions could undermine Nigerians’ freedom to choose their leaders. Comparing the political rhetoric of successive presidents, Turaki recalled former President Goodluck Jonathan’s declaration ahead of the 2015 election that his ambition was not worth the blood of any Nigerian. He contrasted this with former President Muhammadu Buhari’s controversial pre-election warning that the country would be soaked in blood if he was prevented from winning, and Tinubu’s reported remarks that elections were not a tea party and victory must be grabbed, snatched and run with. item.title: FG secures $200m World Bank funding to boost fish production
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has secured a $200 million World Bank-backed financing commitment to boost fish production across the country through state governments, as part of efforts to reduce import dependence and strengthen Nigeria’s aquaculture industry. The funding, to be made available to state governments as concessional loans, is expected to support investments in fisheries and aquaculture, expand production capacity and create opportunities for private-sector participation. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, disclosed this at a high-level executive training on the Aquaculture Investment Guide organised by the ministry in collaboration with the World Bank Group in Abuja. Oyetola, who was represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Marine and Blue Economy, Prof. Busayo Fakinlede, said the financing would help states unlock their fisheries potential and develop commercially viable aquaculture projects. The minister, in a statement issued by his Special Adviser, Bolaji Akinola, said the Federal Government was prioritising collaboration with state governments, investors and development partners to position Nigeria as a fish-sufficient nation. He said expanding domestic fish production had become imperative to address the widening gap between local supply and consumption. According to him, the involvement of state governments is critical to achieving the country’s fish production targets. “Fish is a pillar of food security, household nutrition and rural livelihoods. No nation can call itself food secure while it imports most of the fish it eats. Our ambition is to produce more, import less and, in time, become a net exporter. That ambition can be achieved only when every state plays its part,” he said. Under the proposed framework, states are expected to identify priority aquaculture value chains, assess investment opportunities, develop bankable projects and commit to measurable contributions towards national fish production. Oyetola said the executive training was designed to equip state policymakers and technical officials with the expertise to translate investment opportunities into viable projects. He said the programme would focus on business models, risk management, environmental safeguards and public-private partnerships. The minister commended the World Bank Group for its support for Nigeria’s marine and blue economy development, particularly in analytical studies, capacity building and the development of the Aquaculture Investment Guide. He also disclosed plans to convene a stakeholders’ roundtable after the training to strengthen engagement with state governments, investors and development partners and establish implementation arrangements for the financing initiative. Meanwhile, Fakinlede said the ministry had increased national fish production from 1.1 million tonnes to 1.4 million tonnes through interventions aimed at strengthening the sector. item.title: NAF redeploys senior officers, appoints new commanders
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has announced a major redeployment of senior officers, appointing new Air Officers Commanding (AOCs), Principal Staff Officers (PSOs) and commanders across its operational commands, training institutions and strategic establishments. The exercise, approved by the Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, on November 7, 2026, takes effect from November 2026. Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement, saying the appointments cover the NAF Headquarters, operational commands, Defence Headquarters, training institutions and other strategic establishments. He said the exercise was designed to align leadership competencies and professional experience with the Service’s evolving operational and institutional priorities. At NAF Headquarters, AVM AK Ademuwagun has been appointed Chief of Transformation and Innovation; AVM IV Ajiboye, Superintendent of Standards and Evaluation; AVM PN Amadi, Chief of Air Intelligence; AVM NN Ananaba, Chief of Operations; AVM AH Bakari, Air Provost Marshal; AVM EE Efiom, Chief of Training; and AVM MS Ibrahim, Chairman, Air Expo and International Liaison. Other appointments at the headquarters include AVM AG Kehinde as Chief of Civil-Military Relations; AVM MA Sulaiman as Chief of Communications and Information Systems; AVM S Peters as Coordinator, Project Implementation Team; and AVM AJ Laoye as Chief of Aircraft Engineering. AVM AY Dari becomes General Manager, Nigerian Air Force Investment Limited Group of Companies, while AVM NS Okoro has been appointed Director-General, AFRDI. New operational commanders At the operational command level, AVM NI Ilo has been appointed Air Officer Commanding, Tactical Air Command; AVM BR Mamman, AOC, Mobility Command; AVM OS Ogunsina, AOC, Logistics Command; AVM MN Onyebashi, AOC, Special Operations Command; and AVM FCS Nwakara, AOC, Ground Training Command. To strengthen operational command structures, AVM JI Ukeh has been appointed Commander, Nigerian Air Defence Corps. Other command appointments include AVM OA Abu as Chief of Staff, Mobility Command; AVM I Subi as Chief of Staff, Special Operations Command; AVM NB Folaji as Chief of Staff, Tactical Air Command; AVM F Ekpah as Chief of Staff, Ground Training Command; AVM ES Odekina as Chief of Staff, Logistics Command; and AVM M Umar as Chief of Staff, Air Training Command. AVM GI Jibia has also been appointed Deputy Force Commander, Operation HADIN KAI. item.title: Navy uncovers 68,175 litres of suspected stolen crude in Rivers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has uncovered approximately 68,175 litres of suspected stolen crude oil at illegal storage and refining sites in Ogbogolo Community, Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers State. The discoveries were made during two separate operations conducted on October 24 and November 7, 2026, by personnel of the Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh under Operation Delta Sentinel. The Director of Information, Nigerian Navy, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the operations followed credible intelligence on illegal petroleum storage and refining activities within the Orashi Forest and adjoining areas. According to him, the naval team, during the October 24 operation, discovered two crude oil storage sites containing four dugout pits, 29 sacks and a 25-litre keg, with an estimated 8,675 litres of suspected crude oil. He said a subsequent operation on November 7 led to the discovery of two illegal refining sites comprising two large and 36 small dugout pits, alongside other storage facilities containing an estimated 59,500 litres of suspected stolen crude oil. Folorunsho said the discovered petroleum products and associated items were handled in accordance with established procedures. He explained that the operations underscored the Navy’s sustained intelligence-led efforts under Operation Delta Sentinel to dismantle illegal petroleum storage and refining infrastructure, disrupt crude oil theft networks and deny criminal elements access to the nation’s natural resources. He added that the Navy would maintain operational pressure in identified areas of criminal activity to support the protection of critical oil and gas infrastructure and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. The Navy, he said, remained committed to sustaining the operations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to combat crude oil theft, disrupt illegal refining activities and protect the nation’s maritime and economic interests. item.title: 2Baba thrills fans at Bongo Flava@30 festival
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku Nigerian music icon, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, thrilled music fans in Mbeya, Tanzania, with an energetic performance at the Bongo Flava@30 anniversary festival. 2Baba was among the headline performers at the festival, held on Saturday, November 7, 2026, at Eden Highlands Hotel in Mbeya, as Tanzania’s music industry marked 30 years of Bongo Flava. The Nigerian singer’s appearance added an international flavour to the celebration, which brought together some of Tanzania’s established music stars to reflect on the growth and influence of the country’s popular music genre. His performance reportedly drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, further demonstrating his appeal to music lovers beyond Nigeria. Other artistes who performed at the festival included Bongo Flava pioneers and established acts such as Mr Blue, Afande Sele, Kalapina, Juma Nature, Gangwe Mob and Chidi Benz. The festival was part of activities marking the 30-year journey of Bongo Flava, a genre that has evolved from a local Tanzanian sound into an influential force in contemporary African music. 2Baba’s participation also highlighted the growing cultural ties between Nigeria and Tanzania, particularly through music and entertainment. Widely regarded as one of Africa’s influential musicians, 2Baba has built a career spanning several decades, with hit songs that have earned him a broad following across the continent. His appearance in Mbeya further underscored the reach of Nigerian music and the growing cross-border influence of African artistes. item.title: Kaduna-Kano rail line ready for December 3 inauguration — APC
item.description: …Kano-Katsina-Maradi project reaches 70% completion The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council has said the Kaduna-Kano Standard Gauge Railway will be inaugurated on December 3, 2026, as the Federal Government accelerates the completion of major railway projects in Northern Nigeria. The council also disclosed that the 203-kilometre Kaduna-Zaria-Kano railway project had reached approximately 90 per cent completion, while the 400-kilometre Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project had attained 70 per cent completion. In a statement on Sunday, signed by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the projects demonstrated President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to expanding railway infrastructure, improving regional connectivity and facilitating the movement of passengers and goods. It said the Kano-Katsina-Maradi project was barely five per cent complete when Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while the Kaduna-Kano railway was less than 30 per cent complete. According to the statement, the Kaduna-Kano railway, an extension of the existing Abuja-Kaduna standard gauge line, will establish a continuous rail connection between Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano, linking major commercial centres in Northern Nigeria. The council said the two projects were recently inspected on the directive of the President by a Federal Government delegation led by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi. It said Adebiyi expressed satisfaction with the quality of construction work, particularly the railway alignment, drainage infrastructure, embankment protection, stone pitching and soil stabilisation. The inspection also included a train test run from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano to assess the completed track infrastructure and passenger comfort. The statement added that Tinubu had directed the immediate resolution of outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues within Kaduna metropolis to facilitate the completion of the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano. It further disclosed that the completed 190-kilometre Jaji-Kano section of the Kaduna-Kano railway and the 250-kilometre Dawanu-Kano-Kazaure-Daura-Katsina section of the Kano-Maradi project would be inaugurated on December 3, 2026. When fully operational, the Kaduna-Kano railway is expected to improve passenger transportation, facilitate commercial activities and provide an alternative to road travel along one of Northern Nigeria’s busiest commercial corridors. Similarly, the Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway is expected to strengthen cross-border transportation and trade between Nigeria and neighbouring Niger Republic. The council reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to completing ongoing infrastructure projects across the country in line with its development agenda. item.title: Ibom Deep Sea Port: NDC questions Tinubu’s fresh approval
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has questioned the latest approval of the proposed Ibom Deep Sea Port by President Bola Tinubu, recalling that the project had earlier received approval under former President Muhammadu Buhari in December 2020. The opposition party accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of making repeated promises on the project without delivering on previous commitments, asking how many times the Federal Government would approve the same port. In a statement on Sunday, signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the NDC recalled that the Federal Executive Council (FEC), under Buhari, had on December 16, 2020, approved the implementation of the first phase of the $4.6 billion Ibom Deep Sea Port project. It said the approval named Bollore/Power China as the preferred bidder and was intended to pave the way for the commencement of construction. The statement, titled, “APC’s Endless Lies and Deceit: How Many Times Will APC Approve Ibom Deep Sea Port?”, followed Tinubu’s announcement of approval for the proposed port during his visit to Akwa Ibom State on November 6, 2026. The NDC also recalled that Tinubu, as the APC presidential candidate, had promised to build the port during the party’s campaign rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on January 30, 2023. Quoting the President’s campaign remarks, the party said he had told supporters: “We will do mechanised farming. We will export food from Akwa Ibom. We will build your seaport.” It, however, accused the APC of failing to fulfil the promise, arguing that the latest announcement amounted to a fresh commitment on a project that had already received federal approval. “In a brazen display of ignorance of statecraft and the elevation of grand deceit as a campaign strategy, President Tinubu, as APC presidential candidate, first promised the port during his 2023 campaign,” the party said. The NDC described the latest announcement as another promise that might not be fulfilled, urging Nigerians to hold the ruling party accountable for its previous commitments. Drawing a comparison with the Federal Government’s electricity supply promises, the opposition party said residents of Akwa Ibom were still waiting for the proposed deep sea port despite the earlier approval. It also urged Nigerians to reject the APC in future elections, declaring that a new Nigeria was possible under the NDC. item.title: Dangote refinery IPO misses 10m investors target
item.description: Aliko Dangote, Chairman of Dangote Industries Limited (DIL), has disclosed that the initial public offering (IPO) of the company’s refinery business failed to meet its target of attracting 10 million investors. Dangote, however, said the offer recorded participation from millions of investors, describing the level of demand as significant despite falling short of the target. He spoke at the 25th annual conference of Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) in Lagos, where he attributed the shortfall to time constraints and difficulties some prospective investors encountered in accessing the offer. The billionaire businessman said the exact number of participating investors was yet to be officially determined. “We cannot tell the figure right away because we have not reported to this, but we’ve gotten an amazing demand from various people,” he said. Comparing the level of participation with other major public offerings, Dangote said the refinery IPO had attracted millions of investors, exceeding the participation recorded in some prominent African and international offers. “If you look at it, the largest participating shareholders, like here now, was I think GTBank. When they did their own, it was 200,000. Okay, we are talking about millions of people that participated,” he said. He cited Kenya’s Safaricom offering, which attracted fewer than 900,000 investors, and Saudi Aramco’s global offering, which recorded about five million investors. “We didn’t hit the 10 million because of time constraint, and a lot of people, they didn’t know how to access,” Dangote said. He described the response as evidence of growing public confidence in investment opportunities and the capacity of African businesses to mobilise domestic capital. “But it’s the shared trust of public enterprise that we have today in Africa, and that’s why people are now beginning to remove that money under their mattresses to go and invest,” he added. The Dangote refinery IPO, tagged ‘The People’s IPO’, offered 4.1 billion shares at N525 each, with a minimum subscription of 10 shares valued at N5,250. The offer opened on September 14 and was subsequently extended to October 27. Before the offer commenced, Dangote had announced a target of 10 million retail investors as part of efforts to broaden ownership of the refinery beyond institutional and high-net-worth investors. Reuters reported that more than two million investors had subscribed through digital channels before the offer closed, while the IPO attracted about N6.4 trillion in orders from Nigerian retail and institutional investors, approximately three times the targeted offer size. Dangote had also disclosed that applications came from 120 countries, including all 54 African countries. item.title: Lagos arrests dismissed operative for impersonation, extortion
item.description: …Taskforce impounds 128 motorcycles in fresh clampdown By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Taskforce has arrested a 36-year-old former operative, Adeyemo Olalekan, for allegedly impersonating a serving official of the agency to seize commercial motorcycles and extort their operators. The suspect, who was reportedly dismissed from the agency several years ago over theft-related misconduct, was arrested on Sunday following a tip-off received through the Taskforce’s official hotlines. The agency said preliminary investigations revealed that Olalekan had allegedly continued to pose as a Taskforce operative despite his dismissal, conducting illegal arrests and demanding money from victims in exchange for the release of their motorcycles. A victim, who became suspicious of his activities, reportedly contacted the agency and subsequently discovered that the suspect was no longer in its employment. Speaking on the arrest, the Chairman of the Lagos State Taskforce, Chief Superintendent of Police (CSP) Adetayo Akerele, said operatives apprehended the suspect while he was allegedly attempting to extort two commercial motorcycle operators whose motorcycles he had unlawfully impounded. Akerele said the suspect had evaded arrest on several previous occasions before his eventual apprehension. He added that the agency had been tracking individuals involved in similar fraudulent activities following repeated complaints from members of the public. The chairman described the impostors as criminal elements who exploit the identity and authority of the Taskforce to unlawfully apprehend motorcycle operators and demand money for the release of their motorcycles. According to the agency, the suspect allegedly targeted brand-new Bajaj motorcycles and motorcycles with engine capacities below 200cc, particularly those operating on highways and other restricted routes. He reportedly confessed to disguising himself as a genuine passenger, approaching unsuspecting motorcycle riders and paying their fares before suddenly identifying himself as an enforcement officer. The suspect would then allegedly threaten to have their motorcycles crushed unless they paid him money. He has since been arraigned before a court on three counts bordering on impersonation, extortion and conduct likely to cause a breach of public peace. The agency said he pleaded guilty to all three charges, while the case was adjourned until December 16, 2026, for facts and sentencing. He was subsequently remanded at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre. Akerele reiterated the agency’s determination to rid Lagos of individuals exploiting its identity to engage in criminal activities, warning that dismissed personnel and other impostors would be made to face the law. In a related development, another suspect previously arrested by the agency in October over alleged impersonation and extortion, Yahaya Salami, also known as Adams, appeared in court. item.title: Lagos seals Surulere church over noise pollution
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has sealed The All Christians Gathering Ministry in Surulere over alleged noise pollution and violations of environmental regulations. The church, located at No. 1, Ishola Street, off Clegg, Surulere, was shut on Sunday following an investigation which reportedly established that its activities violated environmental regulations and constituted a nuisance to residents. The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, announced the closure in a statement on his X account, saying the action followed a complaint by a resident identified as DAVERY (@BigDavery) over persistent noise from the church. “Following a complaint by @BigDavery regarding noise pollution from a church, our officials conducted an investigation and confirmed that the church was in violation of environmental regulations and constituted a nuisance to residents in the area,” Wahab said. He added that the facility had been sealed and would remain closed until further notice. The commissioner said the state government would not tolerate environmental violations or activities that disrupted the peace and well-being of residents, stressing that religious institutions, businesses and other establishments must comply with environmental regulations. The enforcement action followed a series of complaints by the resident, who had taken to X in the early hours of Saturday to report noise which he said had repeatedly disrupted his sleep. In one of his posts, made at about 1:31 a.m., the complainant appealed to Wahab to intervene, sharing videos of the noise and offering to provide the church’s address privately for security reasons. In earlier posts, the resident also alleged that a member of the church had threatened him after he confronted the ministry over the noise. He further expressed concern about the impact on other residents, including a household with a child under one year old. The complainant also said the noise had forced him to keep his windows shut at night despite the heat and lack of electricity to operate a fan. The closure forms part of the Lagos State Government’s efforts to enforce environmental regulations and curb noise pollution across the state. Under Lagos State environmental regulations, permissible noise levels in residential areas are 55 decibels during the day and 45 decibels at night. item.title: Rivers: Tinubu, Wike committed to development, says Dike
item.description: By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Rivers State, Barr. Princewill Dike, has described Saturday’s Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, Port Harcourt, as a defining moment in the state’s political history. Dike, who spoke with journalists shortly after the rally, said the event demonstrated political unity and the commitment of Rivers leaders and supporters to the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027 and other Rainbow Coalition candidates in the state. He said the turnout of political leaders, party members, supporters and residents from across the state reflected the level of political mobilisation and support for Tinubu’s administration and the political leadership of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike. Dike said Tinubu’s remarks on the country’s economic challenges and ongoing reforms showed the Federal Government’s determination to address structural problems inherited from previous administrations. “Tinubu is not the cause of Nigeria’s economic woes, but he is not resting on his oars in correcting the economic mismanagement of past administrations,” he said. The APC chieftain urged Nigerians to assess government policies within the broader context of national recovery and sustainable development. He said the President’s response to concerns about hunger and the rising cost of living underscored the need for deliberate reforms, responsible leadership and collective sacrifice. Dike also commended Wike for the mobilisation at the rally, describing him as a political leader whose organisational capacity, grassroots connections and understanding of Rivers politics had attracted national attention. He said Wike’s reference to the completion of the Bonny-Bodo Road, the establishment of the Federal University of Environment in Ogoniland and the appointment of at least 47 Rivers indigenes to federal positions highlighted the importance of engagement with the Federal Government. He also described Wike’s challenge to former Governor Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi to account for projects and financial transactions during his administration as significant, adding that accountability remained an essential element of democratic leadership. Dike further described Governor Siminalayi Fubara’s pledge to deliver at least three million votes for Tinubu in 2027 as a major expression of political commitment. He said the warm embrace between Tinubu and Fubara after the governor’s address symbolised reconciliation and the willingness of political leaders to work together despite previous disagreements. He urged Rivers residents, particularly youths, women and community leaders, to sustain their engagement in the political process ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Asaba rally turns deadly as Delta govt, Omo-Agege trade blame
item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume THE Delta State Government and the Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, have traded accusations over the violence that erupted in Asaba on Saturday during a campaign rally by supporters of the party, leaving one person dead, several others injured and more than 30 vehicles vandalised. While the state government blamed the organisers of the rally for allegedly disregarding security advice from the police, Omo-Agege accused government-sponsored thugs of attacking the campaigners. The Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Mr Charles Aniagwu, in a statement, condemned the violence, describing the incident as unfortunate and warning that the government would not condone political violence or thuggery in the state. Aniagwu said the police had advised the organisers to shelve the proposed street march and relocate their campaign to a designated venue where adequate security arrangements could be provided. According to him, the organisers allegedly ignored the advice, resulting in a confrontation that claimed a life and left several people injured, while vehicles were damaged. He further called on the police to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice. However, Omo-Agege, a former Deputy President of the Senate, insisted that the NDC campaigners were attacked by thugs allegedly sponsored by the state government. In a statement by his Special Adviser on Strategy and Communications, Mr Godwin Anaughe, the former senator described the incident as an act of terror, alleging that it was not the first time NDC members had come under attack during political campaigns in the state. He recalled an alleged attack on members of his party in September this year along Airport Road in Uvwie Local Government Area when some members of his party were attacked during a rally. Omo-Agege also identified some persons allegedly involved in Saturday’s attack and appealed to President Bola Tinubu to prevail on the Delta State Government to demonstrate democratic tolerance as the country approaches next year’s general elections. He said the campaign, which attracted young people and professionals under the Obidient/OK Movement, began peacefully, with participants singing and promoting the political message of Mr Peter Obi and Dr Rabiu Kwankwaso, of the NDC. According to him, the rally remained peaceful for about 20 minutes before armed thugs allegedly descended on the unarmed participants. item.title: Controversy: We didn’t negotiate N40,000 pay adjustment for federal workers—NLC
item.description: *Explains wage increase negotiation done by public sector unions By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has distanced itself from the negotiation of the N40,000 consequential adjustment granted to federal workers, insisting that the responsibility rested solely with the leadership of public sector unions and not the national labour centre. The Congress said the widespread attribution of the N40,000 across-the-board addition to its leadership was misleading, accusing unnamed opponents of the trade union movement of deliberately distorting the collective bargaining process to misinform Nigerian workers and the general public. In a statement yesterday by its Acting General Secretary, Benson Upah, the NLC explained that while it negotiates the national minimum wage through a tripartite arrangement involving government and employers, consequential adjustments are negotiated separately by unions in their respective sectors. The statement reads: “The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has observed with grave concern the deliberate spread of falsehood and mischievous misinformation by certain opponents of the trade union movement and enemies of the Nigerian working class regarding the 2024 national minimum wage setting exercise and the consequential adjustment process. This is issued to educate the public, set the records straight, and expose the ignorance and mischief of those who seek to mislead Nigerian workers and the masses. “For the purpose of clarity, we state that the national minimum wage is set through a tripartite process involving the labour movement, the government, and employers’ representatives. The NLC’s mandate at this stage is clear and unambiguous: to negotiate the national minimum wage; the primary and basic floor below which no worker should be paid. This is the foundational wage upon which all other wage structures are built. “Once the national minimum wage has been agreed upon through the tripartite process, the responsibility for negotiating consequential adjustments; the process of aligning existing wage structures with the new minimum wage, and falling to the respective sectors. This is a fundamental principle of collective bargaining that we cannot belabour here. “In the public sector, the Joint Public Service Negotiating Council (JPSNC), comprising governmentt representatives and approximately eight trade unions with their national leadership, sit with the federal government to negotiate implementation and consequential adjustments. Its state-level counterparts negotiate with state governments. In the private sector, industrial unions negotiate individually with employers’ associations according to the dynamics of their respective sectors. “For example, the Association of Food, Beverage and Tobacco Employers (AFBTE) negotiates with the National Union of Food, Beverages and Tobacco Employees (NUFBTE) on how the national minimum wage will be applied in the food and beverage sector. item.title: Flamingos’ Victory Not A Fluke, Performance Reflects Years Of Development – Coach Busari
item.description: Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari has praised his players for their resilience and tactical discipline after their impressive campaign at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, while expressing optimism about African football’s future. Busari in a post-match interview, said the performance of African teams at the tournament reflected growing quality, character and competitiveness, despite the challenges posed by strong opposition. The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. He noted that the Flamingos had competed in a difficult group that included the defending champions, adding that the experience demonstrated the progress being made in African women’s youth football. “What we are seeing now is not a fluke. It is about development, it is about character, and it is about fighting from the beginning to really get it right. So we are elated and happy,” he said. The coach also expressed hope that more African teams would progress beyond the knockout stages in future editions of the competition and eventually reach the final. Reflecting on the Flamingos’ encounter with Japan, Busari explained that his technical crew had identified the Japanese team’s strength in winning second balls and exploiting spaces behind defensive lines. ﻿ He said the team adjusted its approach to limit Japan’s attacking opportunities, particularly by directing long balls into spaces rather than areas where the opposition could easily gain possession. Busari explained that the Flamingos initially sought to score early before adopting a more cautious approach after taking the lead, but Japan eventually found an equaliser through a set-piece situation. He described the encounter as a tactical contest that required collective defending, discipline and effective game management. According to him, the final stages of the match presented additional challenges as fatigue and anxiety began to affect the young players. Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari celebrating the victory over Japan in the finals of the U-17 World Cup at Rabat on Saturday “The young girls are tired. We have to manage their mental scenario at that point in time. We have to manage the tactics where they need to just hustle for the ball, play fewer touches and play to the zones where the Japanese are less at home,” he explained. He identified dedication, determination and discipline as key principles that guided the team’s approach. “We need to play to our own strengths, not to the opposition’s strengths. Because if we open the game, they are quicker and they can get more one-v-ones,” he said. The coach added that the Flamingos deliberately pressed Japan to force long balls, which would give them opportunities to recover possession and launch attacks. item.title: Lagos Governorship Debate Holds At 7 P.M. Today
item.description: The Nigeria Debate Consortium, a series of debates for the 2027 general elections in Nigeria, will begin today with the Lagos governorship debate. ﻿ It is the first debate in the series, organised by the consortium, which comprises Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper, in selected battleground states ahead of the 2027 elections. The series will end with a presidential debate/townhall. ﻿ The Lagos debate will hold at 7:00 p.m. at The Hub by IALA, House of His Glory, Plot 18, Providence Road, beside Keystone Bank, Marwa, Lekki, Lagos State. The major contenders for the Lagos governorship seat include incumbent Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), and Funso Doherty of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). It added that all participating candidates would be subject to the same rules, speaking times and moderation standards. item.title: Ibom Deep Sea Port: Gov Eno Hails Tinubu’s Approval, Projects Economic Transformation
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s approval of financing arrangements for the Ibom Deep Sea Port as a defining moment in the state’s economic development. He stated this in a statewide broadcast following the President’s visit to Akwa Ibom on Friday, November 6, during which he announced approval for the project. Governor Eno said the deep seaport would serve as a gateway to economic transformation, opening up opportunities in international trade, investment, industrial growth and employment. He expressed confidence that the project would reposition Akwa Ibom as a major economic and maritime hub in Nigeria and the Gulf of Guinea. Governor Eno thanked President Tinubu for his confidence in the state and commitment to national development, assuring him of the Akwa Ibom State Government’s full cooperation towards the successful realisation of the project. ﻿ He described the approval as a significant step in the state’s economic journey and said the government recognised the responsibility that came with the opportunity. The governor also commended residents for their participation in the President’s visit, noting that the reception reflected Akwa Ibom’s reputation as a peaceful, welcoming and investment-ready state. He expressed appreciation to traditional rulers, religious leaders, political stakeholders, youths, women, security agencies, public servants, students and other groups who contributed to the successful hosting of the President. On the forthcoming 2027 general election, he pledged that Akwa Ibom people would support President Tinubu at the polls on January 16, 2027, as part of efforts to ensure continuity in the administration beginning May 29, 2027. He ended the broadcast by thanking the President for his support and urging residents to remain committed to the state’s development, declaring: “Together, we will ARISE, build and prosper.” The post Ibom Deep Sea Port: Gov Eno Hails Tinubu’s Approval, Projects Economic Transformation appeared first on Channels Television .
